messages.author: 7f9a35501eadc0b8
messages.subject: Confidence Interval Length?
parts:
Dear Karl

In general I was wondering what influences the length of a confidence interval for a certain QTL?

A case that I am having (see attachment): On Chr1 I am finding only one significant peak (towards the start of the Chr), but it seems as if (based on the scan plot) two additional peaks are further there (more to the end of the Chr). However they are not significant. Could such a situation stretch my confidence interval, as the confidence interval I am currently getting for the significant peak using the Bayes credible interval, stretches over more then 80% of the whole chromosome?

Thanks for your help.

Best,

Mark

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Confidence Interval Length?
parts:
If there's a second QTL on a chromosome, it could lead to a much wider confidence interval. You could use addqtl() to investigate the evidenc for a second QTL on the chromosome.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Confidence Interval Length?
parts:
Hi Karl (and Mark),

Sorry to butt in here, but I have similar questions. 

What effect does having multiple QTL on a chromosome (stepwise results) have on the reliability of estimates of Bayesian Credible intervals?

What about subtle epistatic effects between different markers on the same chromosome (visible in scantwo plots, but don't survive the stepwise procedure)?

In the book on p 119 It says that intervals assume a priori that the QTL could occur anywhere on the chromosome. For the cases I describe above, is this accounted for, or is this a violation of these assumptions? 

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Confidence Interval Length?
parts:
These confidence intervals for QTL location are derived under the assumption that there is a single QTL; their behavior in the presence of multiple QTL is not well understood.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Confidence Interval Length?
parts:
Thanks Karl. 

Can you recommend a citation to that effect? Or could I cite this as pers comm? 

I'm trying to determine if 2 QTL from different experiments (same RIL linkage map) are the same or not. The QTL are very close (within 3.4 cM), but the 95% Cred. intervals do no overlap. In one experiment there is a single QTL on the chromosome, in the other, there are 2 QTL on the chromosome, plus the subtle epistatic effects. I'm trying to argue that they are the same in spite of the CI (based on a summed lod approach), but it would be good to have cite an expert.

Cheers,

Chris

It's best not to look at overlap of confidence intervals as evidence for/against a common QTL. Ideally, compare a combined analysis to the separate analyses.

karl

messages.author: 7f9a35501eadc0b8
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Confidence Interval Length?
parts:
Dear Karl

I have again a question regarding multiple QTLs on the same chromosome.

You mentioned that the behaviour of confidence intervals isn't well understood in case of presence of multiple QTLs on the same chromosome. 

Does it therefore make sense to try and calculate confidence intervals for each QTL in case one has evidence of the presence of multiple QTLs on the same chromosome? Is this possible at all? If yes, how does one get for example two confidence intervals for two QTLs on the same chromosome, as currently if running for example bayesint() the output is always one confidence interval, even if I have two significant peaks.

Thanks for your help.

Cheers,

Mark
